inputs.text: Health workers in Nigeria are courageously standing up for their labor rights and against these controversial reform bills that would deepen systemic inequality in healthcare. On Thursday, members of the Joint Health Sector Unions and the Assembly of Healthcare Professional Associations marched through Abuja to protest the legislation in the National Assembly. They gathered at the Unity Fountain in Maitama, opposing changes that weaken labor protections and shift priorities away from the needs of ordinary people. This push from those in power is a clear move to entrench institutional interests over the vulnerable, building on historical divides that have long restricted access to care for marginalized communities. Frontline staff and the patients they serve are left more exposed to exploitation and neglect. True progress requires protecting workers and pursuing structural reforms rooted in social justice, not top-down changes that benefit the powerful at everyone else's expense.
